The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Michael Saylor hints at first bitcoin purchase in two months as bitcoin nears $79,000. Bitcoin rebounds from Friday’s low as Strategy’s valuation expands and bitcoin dominance climbs above 60%. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

From Hawala to Swift: Inside the 1,000-year battle to move money safely. Finance has spent centuries decoupling wealth from physical transport, but constantly erasing friction creates vectors for increasingly high-tech exploits. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto market makers are cashing in on bitcoin's rally - without betting on direction. As bitcoin surges back above $80,000, sophisticated trading firms are quietly collecting yield rather than making directional bet. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

A $1.1 million crypto card hack crashed a neobank's token 49%. The exploit caused the neobank's AVICI token to drop 49% from a 24-hour high, hitting a record low before paring some of the losses. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Ditching 'digital gold': BPI study suggests everyday Americans prefer control and micro-investing. A new survey suggests some of bitcoin's most familiar sales pitches of changing the world may be poorly suited to a majority of prospective buyers. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Inside the high-stakes battle between digital dollars and Swift's massive money engine. Crypto executives say new blockchain payment infrastructure could make Swift obsolete. Bankers say its 11,500-institution network gives it the power to absorb the technology instead. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $79,004 with a +1.35% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,504.59 with a +2.29% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

4 min read

In Bitcoin ETF news today, BTC traded near $79,500 on August 28, up +1.1% over 24 hours, as US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) posted $242.30M in net inflows on August 27, extending their streak to nine consecutive trading sessions. [...] The scale gap between the flagship categories and the smaller funds is stark. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, IBIT, contributed $209M of a $338M Bitcoin ETF inflow on August 24.

Its Ethereum fund, ETHA, added $90.92M of that day's $116 million Ethereum ETF haul. Those figures exceed the combined reported totals for Solana and Hyperliquid on August 27.

items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation in the United States has historically been fragmented, with federal agencies applying different interpretations based on the nature and use of each asset. That splintered approach began to change in 2025, when Congress passed legislation to establish a clearer framework for stablecoins and digital asset markets.

## Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs [...] Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. [...] In the U.S., landmark legislation enacted in July 2025 has begun defining the roles of federal agencies in regulating stablecoins and digital commodities. Although implementation is ongoing, these laws represent a shift away from case-by-case enforcement and toward a structured national policy.

items.title: Geopolitical Conflict and Impact on Global Markets
items.description: Geopolitics refer to events that influence the global landscape, including political or trade tensions and military conflicts. Such events often create economic uncertainty, which can lead to fluctuations in stock prices, interest rates, and currencies. Geopolitical conflicts frequently impact supply chains, such as Iran’s threats to halt oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Wars in agricultural regions can also affect crop yields and deliveries. Events like these can cause supply-demand [...] History does not guarantee a quick recovery from every geopolitical shock, and markets can remain volatile when conflict disrupts essential supplies or broadens into the economy. Still, investors have often moved past the first wave of selling once they could assess the likely effects on growth, inflation and profits. A diversified portfolio and a clear investment plan can help investors participate when markets recover from the early negative impacts of major geopolitical events.
